title: Predictors of Running-Related Injuries Among 930 Novice Runners: A 1-Year Prospective Follow-up Study
authors: Nielsen RO, Buist I, Parner ET, Nohr EA, Sørensen H, Lind M, Rasmussen S
population: Novice runners given GPS watches and a neutral shoe, followed for 1 year
findings: 254 of 930 novice runners sustained a running-related injury over 155,318 km of running.

After 500 km, TASRI Type B (non-competitive) behaviour was a significant predictor (cIRD 11.9%, P = .04); age 45-65 (cIRD 14.7%, P = .08) and previous non-running injuries (cIRD 11.1%, P = .05) were clinically interesting but not statistically significant.
BMI groups showed a borderline relationship (P = .06); no significant relationships for sex (P = .42), previous running injury (P = .47), running experience (P = .30) or other sports (P = .30).

The authors suggest BMI over 30 kg/m2, age 45-65, non-competitive behaviour and previous non-running injuries are associated with higher risk, and BMI under 20 was protective; causal roles need investigation.
limitations: Most associations were borderline or non-significant with wide intervals; behaviour questionnaire (TASRI) is unusual; novice sample from one Danish cohort. Running experience was not a significant predictor here, unlike in NLstart2run.
implications: Use age 45-65, BMI over 30 and prior non-running injury as soft risk flags only; evidence is borderline.
Do not treat sex or prior running injury as risk modifiers on this evidence.
Expose cumulative running distance (km) as the injury-risk time scale when modelling novice risk.
